synopsis: HiTac-WAM attaches an explicit contact–deformation–slip forecast to each action candidate generated by a pretrained world action model. Touch affects candidate selection and execution monitoring through a directed tactile branch. The strongest controlled comparison improves robot success using tactile ranking at a fixed candidate budget; forecast accuracy and anomaly detection retain important evaluation gaps.

problem.text: Visually plausible grasping, erasing, or insertion rollouts can conceal missed contact, insufficient pressure, slip, and jamming. The problem is to predict each unexecuted action chunk’s tactile consequences, choose among candidates, and notice when the chosen forecast diverges from physical execution.

contributions.text: A shared multimodal backbone supports a directed tactile pathway with deterministic contact, deformation, and slip heads, imposing explicit downstream conditioning rather than merely sharing features.
The same temporally aligned forecast is used prospectively for candidate ranking and subsequently as a reference for corrective replanning.

inputs: Synchronized RGB history, robot state, language instruction, and bilateral tactile history
Candidate H-step, seven-dimensional action chunk and its generated visual future
outputs: Bilateral future contact estimates, contact-gated 3D deformation fields, and contact-gated slip risk
Selected action chunk; execution-time discrepancy score and a retreat/replanning trigger

steps.name: Condition touch on each candidate
steps.detail: FG-CLTP encodes tactile history into projected tokens. Tactile queries access tactile history and the candidate’s video–action context; visual/action queries cannot attend to tactile keys or values. Action at offset h−1 conditions the tactile target at h. Thus touch evaluates candidate consequences within the shared backbone.

steps.name: Predict the physical hierarchy
steps.detail: Contact is predicted first. Its detached intermediate transition feature conditions a deformation-increment head; detached contact estimates and ungated future-deformation magnitude condition slip. Predicted contact gates both physical outputs. Training supervises the ungated increment and slip probability, while control consumes gated outputs. Shared trainable tactile features still couple the heads despite detached conditioning.

steps.name: Rank valid candidates
steps.detail: Independent noise draws generate candidates; kinematic checks discard invalid chunks. One batched tactile evaluation supplies phase-inconsistent contact, excessive/imbalanced deformation, and peak-plus-mean slip costs. A visual-rollout task-progress estimate rewards advancement. All four components are normalized to [0,1] before weighting.

training.text: Each task has 200 episodes, split into 160/20/20 training/validation/test episodes before window extraction. At 30 Hz, tactile history uses offsets [−12,−6,−2,0], actions 0–23, and targets 1–24. The platform is IMETA-Y1 with bilateral DM-Tac W2 sensors, two RealSense D435i cameras and one USB camera.

Updated components are tactile projections/queries, action–tactile fusion, and tactile heads; a complete freeze map is not given. Each task trains separately for 10,000 steps on eight NVIDIA H100 GPUs with AdamW, learning rate 10^{-4}, and global batch 64. Onset/release weights are 2/1, positive-slip weight 30, and slip-loss coefficient is zero for 3,000 steps then 0.01.

inference.text: Selection and Full use K=4 and progress/contact/deformation/slip weights (1,1,1,0.5). Full executes an eight-step prefix, checking causal tactile observations against aligned predictions. A task-specific KDE fitted on standardized successful-validation residuals scores deviation. Three consecutive threshold exceedances abort remaining prefix actions, trigger safe retreat and fresh observation, and regenerate candidates; at most two corrections are allowed per trial.

equations.expression: \begin{aligned}\widehat C&=\sigma(f_C(z,a)),\\\Delta\widehat{\mathbf D}&=f_D(z,\operatorname{sg}(z^C),a),\\\widehat{\mathbf D}&=\widehat C\odot(\mathbf D_t+\Delta\widehat{\mathbf D}),\\\widehat p^{\mathrm{slip}}&=\sigma\!\left(f_R\!\left(z,\operatorname{sg}(\widehat C),\operatorname{sg}(\|\mathbf D_t+\Delta\widehat{\mathbf D}\|_2)\right)\right),\\\widehat R^{\mathrm{slip}}&=\widehat C\widehat p^{\mathrm{slip}}.\end{aligned}
equations.explanation: Equation (3), for one candidate, offset and sensor: z is its tactile feature, a the aligned action, z^C the contact-head transition feature, and D_t the current grid deformation relative to the undeformed grid. The learned increment predicts change from the current grid. Sigma is sigmoid; sg stops gradients; the contact estimate broadcasts over grid coordinates. Each grid point has two in-plane and one normal displacement components.

Equation (4): contact loss combines binary cross-entropy with onset/release timing losses. Deformation loss is a Huber penalty on increments, averaged over ground-truth-contact offsets/sensors with a positive denominator stabilizer. Slip uses class-weighted binary cross-entropy on the ungated probability. Beta schedules the slip contribution.

Equation (5): k indexes a candidate, rho_task measures predicted task progress, J_C/J_D/J_R are contact/deformation/slip costs, and w terms are weights. The minimum-score k* is selected from kinematically valid candidates. Contact is penalized when inappropriate, rather than universally discouraged.

Equation (6): i is the executed offset, d combines bilateral absolute contact/slip errors and Top-20 normal-deformation MAE, std_task uses validation statistics, and p_KDE is the successful-validation residual density. Persistent S above the task threshold triggers correction; predicted slip alone is not that detector.

results.task: Future tactile prediction on held-out episodes
results.setting: Three task-specific test sets, 20 complete episodes each; 24-step targets. Table II means are unweighted across tasks.
results.metric: Contact F1; onset/release MAE; 3D L2; Top-20 Z MAE; norm ratio; slip AUPRC
results.comparison: Task contact F1 spans 0.908–0.931. Slip prevalence/chance reference is 0.0139.
results.interpretation: Forecast quality is measured on held-out recorded sequences. Deformation metrics use ground-truth-contact frames; AUPRC measures ranking, not probability calibration or robot success.

results.setting: Matched training budgets; separately trained ablation rows in Table III and cumulative conditioning in Figure 5.
results.comparison: Deformation-only: 0.068 mm (17.6% relative error reduction); slip-only: 0.154 AUPRC (60.4% relative increase). Independent-head F1 is 0.896 versus 0.903 contact-only.
results.interpretation: Sharing alone does not consistently improve prediction. Table III’s 0.056 mm is distinct from Table II’s 0.058 mm; the caption explicitly permits differences between independently trained rows.

results.setting: Table I: 30 trials per method/task across chip grasping, blackboard erasing and USB insertion; 360 trials total.
results.value: Full: 76.7/90.0/50.0 by task; average 72.2. Selection: 70.0/73.3/40.0; average 61.1.
results.interpretation: These are executed robot outcomes. Selection gains 30.0 percentage points over single-candidate DreamZero but also uses more candidates; Full adds verification and corrective attempts.

results.setting: K=4 in both arms, matched candidate seeds and validity rules; independent executions, 90 trials per arm. Tactile arm reuses Table I Selection trials.
results.interpretation: This descriptive comparison better isolates the ranking signal from candidate count. It is not an additional independent replication of Selection.

results.setting: Post-hoc recording inspection of 90 Full trials, without exhaustive anomaly annotation.
results.metric: Triggers, anomaly-associated triggers and subsequent completions
results.value: 18 triggers; 16 coincided with anomalies; 12 of those were followed by success; two false triggers had no observed outcome effect.
results.comparison: Full averages 72.2% versus Selection’s 61.1%. At most three of 21 untriggered failures involved an undetected anomaly.
results.interpretation: Useful descriptive recovery evidence, but not a controlled detector sensitivity estimate or proof that all 12 completions were caused by correction.

results.task: Preservation of video and action predictions
results.setting: Comparison with the world action model without tactile prediction, Section V.B.
results.metric: Relative change in video LPIPS and normalized action-trajectory MAE
results.value: LPIPS is 1.4% higher; action MAE is 0.9% higher.
results.comparison: Reference is the WAM without the tactile prediction pathway; absolute metric values are not supplied in this comparison.
results.interpretation: The reported differences indicate modest degradation on these preservation metrics. They do not establish identical outputs, unchanged runtime, or a throughput bound.

limitations.text: The authors explicitly leave forecast quality on model-generated action chunks unevaluated separately and predicted slip risk uncalibrated for online detection.

Experiments cover three tasks on fixed hardware with task-specific training/calibration. They do not establish cross-task or sensor transfer, long-horizon autonomy, or real-time throughput. Detector evidence relies on post-hoc inspection, and the fixed-budget ranking comparison is descriptive.

reproduction.text: Reproduction needs synchronized bilateral grids, contact/slip labels, action alignment, episode-level splits, the pretrained WAM and FG-CLTP encoder, plus successful validation episodes for KDE calibration. Recover exact label thresholds, onset/release loss definitions, cost/progress implementations, KDE bandwidth/threshold values, and safe-retreat parameters: the supplied method gives their roles without a complete executable specification.

reasoning.text: The shared backbone and directed attention support the recorded One Model architecture; this judgment rests on information flow, not joint training alone. The tactile contribution performs forward forecasting, candidate ranking and online verification, making Other mechanisms/Outside quadrants plausible for that layer, although the underlying WAM jointly generates video and actions. Multimodal tactile sensing is directly supported. Policy post-training & WM-RL is only partly supported by task-specific supervised adaptation: no reinforcement-learning objective is described.

discussionQuestions: Would the hierarchy still rank candidates well when their contact states differ substantially from recorded training trajectories?
How much of Full’s improvement survives equalizing recovery attempts and execution time across monitoring baselines?

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title/author/affiliation block and arXiv margin stamp
evidence.detail: Exact title and six authors: Chao Xue, Chaofan Zhang, Wenxuan Ma, Guocai Yao, Shaowei Cui, Shuo Wang. Affiliations are Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences; ImprintX Robotics; Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence. Stamp identifies arXiv:2608.19574v1 [cs.RO], 20 Aug 2026.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 1–2, I. Introduction and Figure 1
evidence.detail: Visually plausible candidates can differ in missed contact, pressure, slip or jamming. The proposed forecast accompanies each action through selection and later execution verification.

History includes RGB, robot state, bilateral touch and language; action chunks are H by 7. FG-CLTP features become tactile tokens. Only tactile queries access the other streams; video/action queries cannot read tactile keys. Listed trainable modules are tactile projections/queries, action–tactile fusion and tactile heads.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, III.B, Eqs. (3a)–(3c); PDF p. 3, Figure 2(b)
evidence.detail: Contact transition features condition deformation; detached contact and ungated future-deformation magnitude condition slip. Contact gates physical outputs. Deformation targets are future-minus-current grids; loss targets are ungated increments/probabilities. Contact interventions substitute learned embeddings indexed by the intervened value.
Joint loss combines contact BCE and timing losses, contact-masked Huber deformation loss, and weighted slip BCE; detached inputs prevent direct slip-loss updates to upstream heads.

Stochastic candidate generation, kinematic filtering and batched tactile prediction precede ranking. Normalized costs encode phase-inconsistent contact, excessive/imbalanced deformation, and peak/mean slip risk, alongside visual task progress.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 4–5, III.D, Eq. (6); PDF p. 7, Figure 7
evidence.detail: Aligned causal observations produce contact/slip absolute residuals and deformation Top-20 Z MAE. Task-standardized residuals are scored by a KDE fitted on successful validation episodes. Persistent deviations abort the remainder, retreat, reobserve and regenerate.

IMETA-Y1, bilateral DM-Tac W2, two RealSense D435i and one USB camera. Each task has 200 episodes split 160/20/20 before windows. At 30 Hz, tactile offsets are −12,−6,−2,0, action offsets 0–23, target offsets 1–24. Deformation labels reference the sensor’s no-contact grid.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, IV.A, right-column training paragraph
evidence.detail: Per-task 10,000-step training uses eight NVIDIA H100 GPUs, AdamW at 10^{-4}, batch 64; onset/release weights 2/1, slip-positive weight 30, and beta 0 for 3,000 steps then 0.01.

Timing MAE uses 30-Hz frames; deformation metrics are restricted to ground-truth contact. Top-20 Z selects points by ground-truth absolute normal deformation; onset variant uses onset frames. Slip prevalence is 1.39%. LPIPS and normalized action MAE assess output preservation.

Each method has 30 trials/task; chip success requires intact delivery and 3 s stability, erasing requires contact and >80% target removal, USB success requires full insertion without sustained jamming plus LED activation. Ranking uses four candidates and weights (1,1,1,0.5). Prefix E=8; three consecutive exceedances trigger correction; at most two corrections. Fixed-budget arms share seeds but execute independently. Detector annotations are post-hoc.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Table I, all task columns and Average
evidence.detail: DreamZero 33.3/50.0/10.0/31.1; Reactive Tactile 40.0/60.0/20.0/40.0; Selection 70.0/73.3/40.0/61.1; Full 76.7/90.0/50.0/72.2 (%). Thirty trials per method/task, 360 total.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table II, all rows; PDF p. 5, Figure 3
evidence.detail: Table II mean F1/onset/release/3D L2/Top-20 Z/norm/AUPRC: 0.921/2.1/2.3/0.058/0.076/0.960/0.247. Task F1 is 0.924/0.908/0.931 and slip AUPRC 0.232/0.251/0.258. Figure 3 presents two representative 24-step forecasts.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table III, caption and all rows; V.B
evidence.detail: Contact-only F1 0.903; deformation-only L2 0.068; independent heads F1/L2 0.896/0.064; contact-conditioned 0.915/0.059; directed hierarchy 0.921/0.056. Hierarchy Top-20 Z 0.072 and norm 0.97. Deformation-only supervision uses contact frames; independently trained rows need not match Table II. Budgets are matched.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Figure 5(a–b) and caption; PDF p. 7, V.B
evidence.detail: GT/predicted/shuffled/zero contact yield L2 0.053/0.056/0.071/0.078 and onset Top-20 Z 0.068/0.072/0.096/0.103 mm. Slip-only/shared-state/contact/deformation cumulative conditioning yields AUPRC 0.154/0.188/0.218/0.247. Contact intervention uses a fixed checkpoint. Error bars are episode-paired bootstrap 95% CIs in (a), stratified episode-bootstrap 95% CIs in (b).

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Figure 6/caption and V.C; PDF p. 6, IV.C
evidence.detail: At K=4, tactile ranking reuses the 90 Selection trials and reaches 61.1%; extra independent task-progress trials reach 35.6%. Matched seeds, task distribution and validity rules; two-sided Wilson 95% intervals are [50.8,70.5] and [26.4,45.8]. DreamZero uses one candidate.

Post-hoc review of 90 Full trials found 18 replanning triggers, 16 associated with anomalies and 12 followed by success; two false triggers had no observed outcome effect. At most three of 21 untriggered failures involved an undetected anomaly. Figure 7 shows one real execution trace, with three consecutive threshold exceedances.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, VI. Conclusion, final paragraph
evidence.detail: The authors state that forecast quality on model-generated chunks is not separately evaluated and slip risk is not calibrated for online detection; controlled anomalies, on-policy adaptation, calibrated uncertainty and learned long-horizon correction remain future work.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, V.B, final sentences; PDF p. 8, VI. Conclusion
evidence.detail: Relative to the WAM without tactile prediction, video LPIPS and action MAE are higher by 1.4% and 0.9%; no absolute values are supplied here. Current-grid/base-grid prior L2 and Top-20 Z are 0.079/0.104 and 0.073/0.099 mm.
